Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{QT}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{RS}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{TR}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RP}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QP}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $P$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QP}=\overset{\to }{QT}+\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RP}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/da5a61cf57c3ffcf82b693b8738334bc840a13b5f34068858e20453906d1b6f2.png)

  

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=a,\,\overset{\to }{TR}=c,\,\overset{\to }{RP}=d.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/c3cb5fabcbd664b0e5eef879cf54f7a5b5d0f187c2f3d68a71d3c91b972005e3.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QP} & =\overset{\to }{QT}+\overset{\to }{TR}+\overset{\to }{RP} \\  & =a+c+d.\end{aligned}
$$
